title: slice-aware canary failure triage and coordinated remediation protocol
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Runbook and orchestration plan for triaging canary failures that selectively impact tenant slices across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments. Goal: provide a fast, repeatable path for identifying slice-correlated regressions, executing targeted mitigations (quarantine, traffic split, live patch), and coordinating customer communications and post-incident actions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Clear triage checklist executed within 20 minutes of first canary signal. 2) Playbook yields either safe auto-fallback to previous model or a targeted quarantine with <= 5 minutes disruption to healthy tenants. 3) Customer comms templates and escalation routing used on at least one production incident during rollout testing.
steps: 1) Signal detection: monitor model quality alerts (eval-regression, hallucination spikes) and runtime anomalies (error / timeout / token deltas) from Console dashboards and SLO monitors. 2) Early slice correlation: run slice diagnostic query (per-tenant traffic distribution, prompt fingerprints, kvcache hit rates) and run eval subset to validate model behavior on failing prompts. 3) Containment: place offending slice(s) onto pinned stable model variant using routing policy; isolate streaming and batching changes, and optionally enable tenant-level throttles. 4) Hotfix options: (A) apply rollout config delta to pin slice to previous stable version, (B) release small parameter-only patch (quantization rollback or logits-thresholding) via live-patch path, (C) reconfigure autoscaler/shard mapping if regression stems from load dysregulation. 5) Verification: run smoke prompts, monitor KV cache reconciliation, and run A/B checks for regressions. 6) Customer comms: open escalation channel, send templated status updates, and provide ETA. 7) Postmortem: capture root cause, revert plan, instrumentation gaps, and remediation PRs.
timeline: T0 (0-20m): Detect & declare slice incident. T1 (20-60m): Correlate and quarantine affected tenants. T2 (60-180m): Deploy targeted fix or pin and verify. T3 (post): Customer follow-up, postmortem, and release retrospective.

- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2748

stakeholders: Oncall (runtime-ops), Serving runtime owners, Customer Success lead, Solutions Engineer for affected tenant, Product Manager (Rollouts)
notes:
- This playbook emphasizes tenant-slice isolation (slice = tenant or tenant cohort) rather than blanket rollback. We prefer minimal surface-area disruption for multi-tenant Dedicated and Private customers.
- Live-patch path is experimental: only permitted for runtime owners with green automated safety tests and agreement from incident manager.
- For Private (on-prem) customers, coordinate with customer-side ops to apply routing changes; include SSH/key rotation checklist when touching KMS or audit logs.
